MADRID, Oct 18 : Kylian Mbappe scored twice as Real Madrid closed the gap on LaLiga leaders Barcelona to six points with a 4-1 win over Sevilla at the Santiago Bernabeu on Sunday, a week before the rivals meet. Arda Guler opened the scoring in the 30th minute, arrowing a shot into the top corner from outside the box, before Mbappe added a second seven minutes later after a brilliant turn. Mbappe won and converted a penalty in the 63rd minute to effectively settle the contest. Sevilla pulled one back with 10 minutes remaining through substitute Manu Bueno, but Yan Diomande restored Real's three-goal lead with a thunderous strike two minutes later. Real climbed to third on 21 points, one behind Atletico Madrid, while Sevilla are sixth on 14.

Source: Reuters

TURIN, Italy, Oct 18 : Lazio's Danish duo made the difference in Turin as Oliver Provstgaard and Gustav Isaksen scored in a 3-0 win over Juventus on Sunday that lifted their side level with Inter Milan at the top of Serie A. Provstgaard broke the deadlock in the 37th minute, using his height to glance home Mattia Zaccagni's cross after Lazio worked a short corner on the left. Fellow Dane Isaksen doubled the lead in the 66th minute, collecting a pass from Tavares on the right before shifting the ball onto his left foot and bending a low finish into the far corner. Fisayo Dele-Bashiru completed the scoring in the 89th minute, launching a counter-attack from inside his own half and driving into the box before slotting home a low finish as frustrated home supporters jeered Juventus through to the final whistle.

Lazio have 19 points from seven matches, level with Inter, who maintained their unbeaten start to the domestic season with a 3-1 comeback victory over Bologna on Saturday. MILAN SURVIVE ATALANTA FIGHTBACK AC Milan survived a late Atalanta fightback to claim an entertaining 3-2 home victory earlier on Sunday. The hosts opened the scoring in the 24th minute through a Goncalo Ramos penalty, before Adrien Rabiot doubled their advantage shortly before the break. Mario Gila made it 3-0 in the 57th minute, seemingly putting the contest beyond Atalanta. However, Gianluca Gaetano reduced the deficit in the 66th minute and Nikola Krstovic added a second for Atalanta in the 81st to set up a tense finish. Two minutes later, Mike Maignan rushed out to deny Davide Zappacosta in a one-on-one, parrying the effort with his legs to preserve Milan's lead. Fiorentina's struggles continued as they suffered a 3-1 defeat at home to Como, leaving them second from bottom in the table with four points from seven matches. Quickfire goals from Mattia Liberali and Nico Paz around the half-hour mark put Como in command before Marin Pongracic pulled one back before the break, but Anastasios Douvikas sealed the victory for the visitors early in the second half. Como are fifth with 14 points.

TAYBEH, West Bank/JERUSALEM: US diplomats visited a Christian Palestinian village in the Israeli-occupied West Bank on Sunday (Oct 18) following attacks by militant Israeli settlers on European diplomats and an American photojournalist in the previous two days. Riley Barnes, assistant secretary of state for democracy, human rights and labor, Brian Burch, US ambassador to the Holy See, and a number of other diplomats visited the Latin Convent church and were expected to meet with members of the Christian community in Taybeh. Belgian, French and Polish diplomats, along with a French mayor and Palestinian civilians, had been attacked near Taybeh on Saturday by masked Israeli settlers. The previous day, Washington Post photojournalist Heidi Levine was taken to hospital after being assaulted while covering a Palestinian olive harvest near another West Bank village.

The diplomats' visit coincided with US President Donald Trump endorsing his ally, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, for Israel's parliamentary election on Oct 27. Meanwhile, US Ambassador to Israel Mike Huckabee attended a settler conference in the West Bank on Sunday. Huckabee, an evangelical Christian and longtime supporter of Israel, earlier wrote on X calling for "those who attacked" the Washington Post photojournalist, a US citizen, to be jailed.

NETANYAHU CIRCUMSPECT ON SETTLER VIOLENCE Trump has expressed his opposition to Israeli annexation of the West Bank, but his administration has put little pressure on Netanyahu's right-wing, pro-settler government to change its policy. UN bodies and most countries deem the settlements illegal under international law, but Israel rejects this, viewing the territory as disputed rather than occupied. While Foreign Minister Gideon Saar and the Israeli military both blamed "Israeli rioters" for the attack on the diplomats, Netanyahu, whose coalition is projected to lose its governing majority, has been more circumspect. He has said the diplomats entered a "sensitive area with a history of confrontations without prior coordination" with the Israeli military, and that the facts of the attack on Levine are "unclear". France urged Israeli authorities to arrest Saturday's attackers and to end criminal violence in the West Bank, but by Sunday there was no announcement from Israeli authorities of any arrests in either of the two latest incidents.

Israeli settlers attack a journalist in Abu Falah, West Bank Oct 16, 2026, in this screengrab from a video. (Photo: Andrey X/via REUTERS)

The West Bank is home to some 500,000 settlers and at least 3 million Palestinian s. Settler attacks on the Palestinian s are surging, with at least 170 since Sep 27, according to Yesh Din, an Israeli human rights group. Journalists, activists and foreign observers have also been targeted. Yet prosecutions of Israeli settlers are rare. On Sunday, Reuters saw a group of at least 10 settlers, masked and dressed in black, hurling rocks at Palestinian s and activists harvesting olives near the Palestinian West Bank town of Salfit, prompting the farmers to flee. Israeli border police were in the area and shot tear gas towards the hills.

Source: Reuters/fs

LONDON, Oct 18 : Arsenal are gaining a reputation as slow starters this season, but their ability to find a way through tight games helped them earn a 1-0 win against Nottingham Forest on Sunday and keep their Premier League title defence on track. Arsenal's total of 11 league goals from seven games is the second-lowest in the top six, eight behind leaders Manchester City and a whopping 12 behind third-placed Brighton & Hove Albion. Eight of those 11 strikes have come after halftime and they again struggled for attacking fluency in the opening 45 minutes against Forest before substitute Noni Madueke's deflected 80th-minute strike secured the points. The goal came from Arsenal's first shot on target and kept Mikel Arteta's side in touch with table-toppers City.

"The longer the game goes on, they have more belief. You have to take more risks, and that's when the game can break," an upbeat Arteta told Sky Sports. Madueke said Arsenal might not have won such a game last season but now possessed greater belief and resilience. "At times maybe last year, this game might have not gone as it did for us in the end, but I think we got that extra belief, that extra mentality now," he said. "We know we're the champions, and we know we can pull out the bag wherever we go, and just delighted that we're able to do it today." Arsenal looked toothless in the first half and although they were sharper after the break, it still took until the 80th minute for Madueke to produce the effort that finally broke the hosts' resistance. The 24-year-old, who came off the bench at the break to replace Eberechi Eze, said Arsenal's squad depth was proving to be one of their main strengths this season.  "If you look at the quality of our starting 11 and bench it's absurd, so we know that we're going to start some and finish some (games) and for me it's the same mentality every time, I just want to create or score. Amazing feeling (to score), but I feel better about the win," he said.  "We have elite players, all 20-something players are elite and of the highest level. It's great to have that type of competition, you know on the bench you're ready to have an impact."

Source: Reuters

Oct 18 : Anthropic said on Sunday it will commit 5 per cent of its shares to a new public benefit fund, subject to stockholder approval, with the stake potentially increasing as the artificial intelligence giant's valuation grows. The proposed fund would be established as a wholly owned limited liability company and would receive an additional 2 per cent of Anthropic's shares, at the board's discretion, for every 50 per cent increase in the company's value above a baseline that has yet to be disclosed. The Anthropic Public Benefit Fund could support initiatives including nonprofit donations, direct distributions to specific populations and efforts to address AI’s impact on workers. The company said none of the equity held by the fund would be used for lobbying or political contributions in the US or abroad.

The maker of the Claude AI assistant is planning one of the biggest IPOs in history as a public benefit corporation, a legal structure that requires management to consider certain broader interests as well as turning a profit for investors. The company, which has positioned itself as safety-first, has often highlighted risks associated with its AI models, most recently in its IPO prospectus, which it said could exhibit "self-preserving behaviors," Reuters reported exclusively in September. Taken together with the new fund, roughly 20 per cent of Anthropic's shares would be dedicated to public purposes, excluding any additional shares that could be allocated if it reaches future valuation milestones. Anthropic said it would disclose further details in coming months on the fund's governance, structure and the valuation thresholds that could expand its ownership stake. It also plans to publish a public-benefit report detailing progress toward its mission.

CALGARY: The Canadian government said on Sunday (Oct 18) that a weekend fire at an Alberta military base killed at least four people and seriously injured dozens in what Prime Minister Mark Carney called one of the worst peacetime tragedies ever for Canada's armed forces on home soil. "The nation is in mourning for those brave members of our Armed Forces whom we have lost," Carney said Sunday, adding that he had ordered flags on federal buildings across the country to be lowered to half-staff to honour the victims. CBC, the government-funded national broadcaster, previously reported seven deaths at Canadian Forces Base Wainwright, citing unnamed sources. Canadian authorities have said the situation continues to evolve, and that they will not confirm casualty figures until next of kin have been notified. CFB Wainwright had 1310 military and civilian personnel stationed there as of 2021, according to census data. The base, one of Canada's largest, is about 210 km east of Edmonton in Alberta. National Defence Minister David McGuinty said on Sunday he would go to the city for briefings on the situation.

The base houses the Canadian Manoeuvre Training Centre, which runs training scenarios and exercises for the army. Carney said those affected in Saturday's fire came from military bases across the country. Few details have been released about the cause of the fire, which took place at about 4pm on Saturday (6am Sunday, Singapore time) in a training area at the base as winds gusted up to 96 kilometres per hour.

People attend a church service, the day after a serious incident that resulted in a fire caused deaths and injuries at Canadian Forces Base (CFB) Wainwright, in Wainwright, Alberta, Canada, Oct 18, 2026. (Photo: REUTERS/Jennifer Gauthier)

Military and civilian firefighters fought the fire through the night in "some of the worst conditions imaginable," Carney said. Canadian officials are expected to address the public from Wainwright, which is located in a largely rural area, later on Sunday afternoon. Air ambulances from Edmonton and Saskatoon, which is about 300 km from Wainwright, flew to the military base on Saturday, Carney said. Patients are being treated in Edmonton, Wainwright, Calgary and Red Deer, he said. Health staff in Edmonton said a "code orange," or mass-casualty event, was declared to coordinate the medical response for patients being transported from Wainwright, CBC News reported. The town of Wainwright, with a population of about 6600, is just north of the base. The municipality posted on social media that the fire had crossed the base fence into the nearby district but no evacuation orders had been issued. It said on Sunday that the fire is not expected to spread beyond its current boundaries.

Source: Reuters/fs

Oct 18 : Eight months after some Brighton & Hove Albion fans called for Fabian Huerzeler to be sacked after a home defeat by Crystal Palace, the young manager has the Seagulls soaring in third place in the Premier League after Sunday's 5-0 rout of the same opponents. The 33-year-old, the youngest manager in the English top flight, watched his side demolish rivals Palace in a game capped by Diego Gomez's spectacular halfway-line strike that sent the home fans into raptures. It was a far cry from February's 1-0 defeat in the "M23 Derby" that left Brighton languishing in 14th place as some of the club's fans chanted "You're getting sacked in the morning." Brighton, however, refused to push the panic button and retained their faith in Huerzeler, who eventually guided the south-coast club to an eighth-placed finish.

Chairman Tony Bloom rewarded Huerzeler with a contract extension until 2029 and the club are reaping the benefits of the trust placed in the young German. LEAGUE-LEADING 23 GOALS With Sunday's 5-0 victory, Brighton sit five points behind leaders Manchester City with a league-leading 23 goals in seven games, five clean sheets and a goal difference of plus 18, six better than City's. "A few months ago (after losing to Palace) we were in a different place and I said I'd keep pushing to get another opportunity to beat them, so I'm happy we did it today," Huerzeler told Sky Sports. "It's not a one-man show, so I credit my players and my staff. Hopefully everyone enjoyed it." While Erling Haaland has scored eight of City's goals to move clear in the Golden Boot race, Brighton have already had 11 different scorers. "If you look, they're shared around a lot which is a massive help. We've got everyone chipping in and helping out the team," Brighton defender Lewis Dunk told BBC Radio. "If you look at our clean sheets, I think it's the most we've ever had at this part of the season, so we're buzzing with that as well." RELENTLESS PRESSING Brighton's success in the new campaign has been built on relentless pressing, a hallmark of last month's commanding 3-0 victory over champions Arsenal that left coach Mikel Arteta searching for answers after his side's first defeat of the season. Pascal Gross's successful return has provided another major boost. The 35-year-old, who previously spent seven seasons at Brighton, rejoined the club earlier this year in search of regular first-team football. Gross is their joint-top scorer with three goals while the German also leads the team with four assists. It was his free kick that forced an own goal in the fourth minute that opened the floodgates against Palace. Dunk refused to entertain talk of a title challenge so early in the season, while Huerzeler was equally determined to keep expectations in check. "To me, the most important thing is the things we can improve... It's good to celebrate the win, but understand there is still space for improvement, especially for individual players," he said. "We have to keep going. We can't be satisfied. We have to keep pushing, stay humble and understand why we are successful at the moment to keep pushing at that level."

WASHINGTON: US President Donald Trump on Sunday (Oct 18) endorsed his ally Benjamin Netanyahu as the longtime Israeli prime minister struggles for an edge in next week's parliamentary election. Trump praised Netanyahu as a "great warrior prime minster" and peace partner, crediting him with joining the United States in launching strikes on Iran in February. The conflict, in its seventh month, has disrupted energy markets globally and wreaked havoc across the Middle East, damaging critical infrastructure and destabilising regional economies. "Bibi Netanyahu has been Strong, Brave, and Brilliant in the face of tremendous opposition, including that coming from even Israel, itself," Trump wrote in a post on Truth Social. "Despite all of that, he has endured and, in fact, he has thrived! I have watched Bibi under the most trying of times. Normal men or women in such situations would have wilted under the pressure — But Bibi did not wilt, he actually got stronger, and maintains that same Strength today."

In his message, addressed to "the Great People of Israel," Trump added, "Please let this Letter serve to represent my Complete and Total Endorsement of Bibi Netanyahu in his upcoming Race for Re-Election as Prime Minister of Israel." The Trump endorsement is not certain to give Netanyahu and his right-wing Likud party a boost in the Oct 27 national election, as Israeli public support for Trump has diminished amid Israeli-US disagreements over Iran.

Polls have suggested no candidate has a clear path to power. Israel's prime minister is chosen through coalition-building in parliament rather than by direct popular vote. It will be Israel's first vote since the Hamas attack on Oct 7, 2023, that shook the country and plunged the Middle East into turmoil, as Israel went to war in Gaza, Lebanon and Iran. The election could determine whether Netanyahu remains in power after one of the most consequential periods in Israel’s history, or is defeated by centrist rivals promising to usher in a new era. Netanyahu promptly expressed his thanks to Trump on X, saying, "Together we will complete the mission!" Trump has broken with longtime US tradition by endorsing candidates in elections in foreign countries, including Hungary, Colombia, Argentina, Japan and Honduras.

LEEDS, England, Oct 18 : Manchester United manager Michael Carrick took heart from his team's resilience in Sunday's 1-1 Premier League draw at Leeds United, but his description of the result as a "step forward" underlined how far expectations have fallen during a difficult spell for the club. One win from seven league games has left United languishing in 13th, a stark contrast to last season's third-place finish and evidence that their problems run deeper than a difficult week. Carrick conceded they had fallen short of the quality they are capable of producing, particularly on the ball, but he found encouragement in the discipline and togetherness his players showed in the pressure of a fierce rivalry at Elland Road. "Maybe if you talk about top quality, maybe it wasn't top, top quality I think we are capable of playing," Carrick said. "With the results we've had we weren't quite flowing but there's enough in there to take from it."

The greater significance for Carrick appeared to lie in how United responded to adversity.  After being outplayed in a 1-1 draw with bottom side Tottenham Hotspur last weekend and losing 2-0 at Atletico Madrid in the Champions League, the build-up to Sunday's game was further complicated by Lisandro Martinez publicly criticising the club hierarchy before apologising. Against that backdrop, Carrick placed greater emphasis on structure than style. United were harder to break down, and he praised his players for sticking to their roles and responsibilities in what he described as a tense game that could have gone either way. "It's a bit more than just effort," Carrick said. "It is the way you go about it. The plan. The responsibilities. The roles. I thought the boys took that responsibility on really well for the most part." FAMILIAR SHORTCOMINGS Yet familiar shortcomings remained. United surrendered their lead from a set piece and lacked enough quality in possession to take control of the match, leaving Carrick with another draw rather than the victory his side badly needed. After a week dominated as much by events off the pitch as those on it, however, Carrick was keen to stress that the dressing room remained united. "I suppose you're looking at the togetherness, the spirit, the unit. I don't doubt that within the group," he said. "The way that we went about it today gives me a lot of belief in us moving forward." United head to Como for a Champions League game on Wednesday.

LEVERKUSEN, Germany, Oct 18 : Bayer Leverkusen netted a 76th-minute winner through leading scorer Patrik Schick to beat Freiburg 2-1 on Sunday and move into the top four of the Bundesliga standings. Czech striker Schick, who became the first Leverkusen player to score in each of the first six matches of a season, tapped in after superb work from Ibrahim Maza, as his team moved to 13 points, behind Freiburg on goal difference. BRIGHTON, England, Oct 18 : Diego Gomez produced a stunning halfway-line goal as Brighton & Hove Albion thrashed Crystal Palace 5-0 on Sunday, the Premier League's longest-range strike in nearly nine years. With Brighton 1-0 up following an early own goal from Jaydee Canvot, Gomez spotted Palace goalkeeper Walter Benitez off his line in the seventh minute and seized his opportunity from the centre circle. The Paraguayan midfielder took one touch before unleashing a spectacular shot from 51 metres out, leaving the backtracking Benitez desperately flailing his arms as the ball sailed over him and into the back of the net. Gomez's audacious strike was the furthest range goal in the Premier League since Wayne Rooney scored for Everton against West Ham United from 58 metres out in November 2017, according to data firm Opta.

Oct 18 : Champions Arsenal needed a late goal from Noni Madueke, their only shot on target, to scrape a 1-0 win at Nottingham Forest on Sunday and remain three points behind Premier League leaders Manchester City. Brighton & Hove Albion's Diego Gomez struck a sensational goal from inside his own half in a 5-0 rout of Crystal Palace on Sunday to leave his side third in the table with 16 points, five behind leaders Manchester City. Manchester United and bitter rivals Leeds United shared the spoils in a 1-1 draw at Elland Road at the end of a turbulent week for the Red Devils in which defender Lisandro Martinez had publicly challenged the club's hierarchy. Leeds are seventh in the table and Manchester United, who have just one win from seven games, are 13th.

Bournemouth beat Sunderland 2-0 for their first league victory of the season to climb to 15th place. Sunderland remained in the drop zone in 19th place. At the City Ground, a frustrated Arsenal finally sealed victory in the 80th minute. Ibrahim Sangare hesitated when he could have cleared the ball, leaving Forest manager Oliver Glasner visibly fuming, and second-half substitute Madueke then danced past Daniel Munoz before hammering a shot that deflected off Jair Cunha and wrong-footed Matz Sels. "We're really happy, we did it all together. We showed grit, determination, and maybe we showed a champion spirit here for that, really pleased," Madueke told Sky Sports. Murillo almost salvaged a point for Forest in injury time when he beat three players before unleashing a shot that sailed agonisingly wide. The defeat left Forest, who have yet to win or even score at the City Ground this season, in the drop zone in 18th place with five points. At the Amex, Brighton got on the scoresheet in the fourth minute through a Jaydee Canvot own goal, before Gomez struck a goal of the season contender three minutes later, robbing Adam Wharton of the ball near the halfway line before taking a touch and firing the ball over keeper Walter Benitez and into the net. "When I got the ball I knew the goalkeeper was a little bit ahead," Gomez told Sky Sports. "When I scored I didn't know where to run or what to do. I was very happy with the goal." Yasin Ayari padded Brighton's lead three minutes later, before Charalampos Kostoulas and Jack Hinshelwood completed the rout after the break. Kostoulas scored just after halftime when Ayari's shot deflected into the Greece international's path, and Hinshelwood struck in the 84th when Luka Vuskovic's header was scooped off the line by Benitez and he fired home the rebound. MBEUMO GRABS OPENING GOAL Manchester United looked on course for a much-needed victory when Bryan Mbeumo scored in the 35th minute after missing a couple of chances. Mbeumo held off James Justin before tapping in a Youri Tielemans cross from six yards out. Leeds striker Dominic Calvert-Lewin equalised in the 51st minute, chesting down the ball from a corner before poking home.  "We are slightly disappointed it is just a point," Leeds boss Daniel Farke told Sky. "Second half, we got the equaliser, we should have kept up the dominance, too many strikes went over the crossbar but it was overall a solid performance. "We took it as a compliment that we have done many things right over the last month if we were seen as favourites against Manchester United." Manchester defender Martinez retained his place in Michael Carrick's starting lineup despite criticising United's hierarchy following Tuesday's 2-0 Champions League defeat at Atletico Madrid, questioning the club’s summer investment and singling out director of football Jason Wilcox before later apologising. Bournemouth punished a shaky Sunderland start to take the lead after just six minutes, when Lewis Cook lofted a long ball forward that Evanilson ran on to and squared for Marcus Tavernier to head home from close range. Evanilson scored himself in the 48th minute when the Brazilian rounded goalkeeper Robin Roefs before slotting home left-footed.

FAST

Oct 18 : Paris St Germain left back Nuno Mendes will be sidelined for weeks after suffering a thigh injury, the Ligue 1 champions said on Sunday, dealing a blow to their preparations for Tuesday's Champions League home game against Barcelona. • The 24-year-old Portugal international sustained the injury during PSG's 3-1 Ligue 1 victory at Strasbourg on Saturday. • "Nuno Mendes, who suffered an injury to his left thigh during last night's match against RC Strasbourg Alsace, will be unavailable for the next few weeks," PSG said in a statement. • Mendes has make seven appearances across all competitions this season. • The back-to-back European champions sit top of the standings with maximum points from their opening two matches. Barcelona are second, also on six points.

Source: Reuters

FAST

Egypt is ready to provide Saudi Arabia with the support it needs to defend its security and stability, the presidency said on Sunday (Oct 18), as Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis intensify their attacks on the world's largest oil exporter. Egyptian President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi requested an urgent parliament session to authorise the military, one of the Arab world's largest, to help defend Saudi Arabia if the kingdom requested its support. A parliamentary vote had been expected on authorizing the request for military support on Sunday, but discussions were due to continue on Monday, two lawmakers and local media reports said. HOUTHIS RAMP UP ATTACKS ON SAUDI ARABIA The Houthis have in recent days attacked Riyadh's international airport and the state oil giant Saudi Aramco, amid renewed fighting with the Saudi-backed forces of the internationally recognised government following the collapse of a truce.

"Egypt will provide Saudi Arabia with all necessary and possible forms of support to defend its security and stability, protect its resources, territorial integrity and Islamic holy sites," the Egyptian presidency said in a statement. It followed a meeting of Egypt's National Defence Council chaired by Sisi and attended by the parliamentary speaker, the prime minister and the army chief. Sisi said in a speech on Saturday that Egypt would act in accordance with guidance from Saudi King Salman and Crown Prince Mohammed Salman, who visited Sisi on Sep 15, after fighting in Yemen reignited. Egypt and Saudi Arabia are close strategic and economic partners. Saudi Arabia and other oil-rich Gulf states provided Egypt with billions of dollars in aid, central-bank deposits and investments after the military ouster of President Mohamed Morsi in 2013. Egypt had previously joined the Saudi-led coalition that intervened in Yemen in 2015 to support the government against the Houthis, but played a limited combat role.
